name: Queen's Gambit
summary: The Queen's Gambit (1.d4 d5 2.c4) offers a wing pawn to lure Black's d-pawn away from the centre. It is not a real gambit: if Black takes, White wins the pawn back with e3/e4 and Bxc4 and keeps the bigger centre. This repertoire meets the Queen's Gambit Declined with 3.Nc3 and 4.Bg5, the Queen's Gambit Accepted with the central 3.e4, and the Slav with 3.Nf3, 4.Nc3 and 5.a4, with clear answers to the Albin, Chigorin, Baltic, Marshall and Symmetrical defences. The games are strategic: White plays for space, pressure on d5 and the c-file, and long-term targets such as an isolated d-pawn or the minority attack.
keyIdeas: 2.c4 attacks d5: Black must give up the centre (2...dxc4) or defend it with ...e6 or ...c6.
If Black takes on c4, win the pawn back with e3/e4 and Bxc4; holding it with ...b5 usually fails to a4.
Against the QGD, pin the f6-knight with Bg5 and put a rook on c1. Black's problem piece is the c8-bishop shut in behind e6.
Isolated d-pawn positions: blockade the square in front of Black's isolated pawn and pile up on it (Bg2, Qb3, Rd1); when the isolated pawn is ours, use the open lines to attack.
In the Exchange structure (our d4/e3 against Black's c6/d5) play the minority attack: b4-b5 to create a weak c6- or d5-pawn.
Against the Slav, 5.a4 stops ...b5, so Black cannot keep the c4-pawn; then e3, Bxc4, O-O, Qe2 and e4.
Against offbeat second moves (Albin, Chigorin, Baltic, Marshall, Symmetrical) take the centre and develop: each has a concrete antidote.
typicalPlans: QGD Orthodox: Rc1, Bd3, Bxc4 after ...dxc4, then if Black frees with ...e5 use the isolated d-pawn for Ne5 and a rook lift (Rc3-g3).
Exchange Variation: Qc2, Bd3, O-O, Rab1, b4, a4 and b5 (the minority attack) against Black's c6-pawn.
QGA with 3.e4: Bxc4, Nf3 or Ne2, O-O, then use the space from e4-e5 or d4-d5 while keeping the centre pawns protected.
Slav main line: e3, Bxc4, O-O, Qe2 and e4-e5 followed by a kingside attack.
Against the Tarrasch: g3, Bg2, O-O, Bg5/Be3, Rc1 and Qb3 against the isolated d5-pawn.
commonMistakes: Grabbing the d5-pawn with Nxd5 when the f6-knight looks pinned: the Elephant Trap (4...Nbd7 5.cxd5 exd5 6.Nxd5?? Nxd5! 7.Bxd8 Bb4+) costs a piece.
Playing 4.e3? against the Albin: 4...Bb4+ 5.Bd2 dxe3! 6.Bxb4?? exf2+ 7.Ke2 fxg1=N+! wins (the Lasker Trap). Play 4.Nf3.
In the Cambridge Springs, an early Bd3?? lets ...dxc4 open the fifth rank, and the a5-queen wins the g5-bishop.
Moving the f1-bishop before Black has taken on c4 in the Orthodox QGD, so that ...dxc4 makes the bishop move twice.
In the Slav, delaying a4 after 4...dxc4: without it, ...b5 makes it hard to win the c4-pawn back.
Playing an early e4 when the e4-pawn is not protected (for example against the Marshall with ...g6), which lets Black's knight take it.

lines.name: QGD Orthodox: Capablanca's Freeing Manoeuvre (7.Rc1 c6 8.Bd3)
lines.description: The classical main line of the Queen's Gambit Declined: we pin with Bg5, put a rook on c1 and develop. Black frees the game with ...dxc4, ...Nd5 and ...e5, and we get an active isolated d-pawn, the open e-file and attacking chances with Ne5 and a rook lift to g3. Other Black moves: 3...Be7 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.Bg5 transposes; 3...Bb4 has its own line; 3...c6 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.e3 is our Semi-Slav line (the Noteboom 4...dxc4 is met by 5.a4 Bb4 6.e3 b5 7.Bd2 and we win the pawn back); 3...h6 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.Bf4 and e3 is a quiet QGD where Bg5 is no longer possible. 4...Nbd7 leads to the Elephant Trap and Cambridge Springs lines; 4...dxc4 5.e3 c5 6.Bxc4 cxd4 7.exd4 gives us an active isolated pawn; 4...Bb4 5.cxd5 exd5 6.e3 is a solid Exchange-type position; 4...c5 is covered in the Semi-Tarrasch line; 4...c6 5.e3 Nbd7 6.Nf3 reaches the Cambridge Springs or Orthodox lines. 5...h6 6.Bh4 O-O 7.Nf3 leads to the Lasker or Tartakower lines; 5...Nbd7 6.Nf3 O-O transposes; 5...b6 6.Nf3 O-O 7.Rc1 Bb7 8.cxd5 is a Tartakower-type position; 5...dxc4 6.Bxc4 (or 6.Nf3 c5 7.Bxc4) and we develop with Nf3 and O-O. 6...h6 is the Lasker/Tartakower; 6...b6 7.Rc1 (or 7.cxd5) is the Tartakower idea without ...h6; 6...c6 7.Bd3 (or 7.Be2) dxc4 8.Bxc4 Nbd7 9.O-O is close to the main line; against 6...dxc4 or 6...c5 just play 7.Bxc4 or 7.cxd5 and keep developing.
lines.evaluation: Roughly +0.4: a pleasant, active position for White

lines.name: Elephant Trap: 4...Nbd7 5.cxd5 exd5 6.Nxd5?? (a trap for White)
lines.description: After 4...Nbd7 the d5-pawn looks like free food because the f6-knight seems pinned. It is not: 6.Nxd5?? Nxd5! 7.Bxd8 Bb4+ and Black gets the queen back and ends up a piece up. Against 4...Nbd7 simply play 5.e3 (see the Cambridge Springs line); 5.cxd5 exd5 6.e3 is also fine. If Black plays 5...h6?! instead of recapturing, 6.Bxf6 Nxf6 7.dxe6 Bxe6 8.Nf3 simply wins a pawn.
lines.evaluation: After 9...Kxd8 Black is a piece up (about -5): avoid 6.Nxd5??

lines.name: Cambridge Springs Defence: 6...Qa5 7.Nd2
lines.description: Black uses the queen on a5 to pin our c3-knight and to eye the g5-bishop along the fifth rank. 7.Nd2 breaks the pin, stops ...Ne4 and gets ready to hit the queen with Nxc4. Watch out: 9.Bd3?? dxc4! wins a piece, because the a5-queen attacks g5 once the d5-pawn is gone (10.Bxf6 cxd3! 11.Qxd3 Nxf6). 7.cxd5 Nxd5 8.Qd2 is a solid alternative. Other Black moves: 5...Be7 6.Nf3 O-O is the Orthodox main line; 5...h6 6.Bh4 Be7 7.Nf3 O-O transposes to the Lasker/Tartakower lines; 5...dxc4 6.Bxc4 and we develop with Nf3 and O-O. 6...Be7 7.Rc1 or 7.Qc2 is a normal Orthodox position; 6...h6 7.Bh4 keeps the pin; 6...Bb4 7.cxd5 exd5 8.Bd3; 6...a6 7.cxd5 exd5 8.Bd3; 6...a5 7.Bd3 dxc4 8.Bxc4. In all of them we castle and fight for e4.
lines.evaluation: Equal to slightly better for White (+0.2)

lines.name: QGD Tartakower: 7...b6 8.cxd5 (Fischer v Spassky 1972)
lines.description: The Tartakower (TMB) system is Black's most solid QGD set-up: ...h6, ...b6 and ...Bb7. With 8.cxd5 and quick swaps we leave Black with 'hanging pawns' on c5 and d5 and attack them, as Fischer did in game 6 of the 1972 world championship. If Black plays 6...b6 without ...h6, use the same idea: 7.cxd5 Nxd5 8.Bxe7 Qxe7 9.Nxd5 exd5 10.Rc1.
lines.evaluation: Equal on the engine (+0.3), but Black's pawns are easy to target

lines.name: QGD Exchange Variation: 7.Qc2 and the Minority Attack
lines.description: A simpler alternative to 4.Bg5: take on d5 at once and play for the minority attack. Our a- and b-pawns (two) advance against Black's a7, b7 and c6 (three) to leave Black with a weak c6- or d5-pawn. 7.Qc2 also stops ...Bf5. lines.name: Tarrasch Defence: 6.g3 Main Line with 9.Bg5
lines.description: Black accepts an isolated d-pawn for free piece play. We fianchetto the bishop to g2, where it stares at d5, blockade on d4 and slowly pile up on the weak pawn. Other Black moves: 4...cxd4 is the Schara-Hennig Gambit: 5.Qa4+ Bd7 6.Qxd4 exd5 7.Qxd5 Nf6 8.Qd1 and we keep the extra pawn; 4...Nf6 5.dxe6 Bxe6 6.Nf3 also keeps an extra pawn. 5...Nf6 6.g3 Nc6 7.Bg2, 5...cxd4 6.Nxd4 Nf6 7.g3 and 5...Be7 6.g3 Nf6 7.Bg2 usually transpose. 6...c4 (the Swedish) is met by 7.Bg2 and 8.O-O followed by e4 or Ne5; 6...cxd4 7.Nxd4 Nf6 8.Bg2, 6...Be7 7.Bg2 Nf6 8.O-O and 6...h6 7.Bg2 Nf6 8.O-O transpose. On move 9, 9...c4 is answered by 10.Ne5 (or 10.e3) and later b3 to break up Black's queenside pawns.

lines.name: Semi-Tarrasch: 4.Nf3 c5 5.cxd5 Nxd5 6.e4
lines.description: If you prefer 4.Nf3 to 4.Bg5, Black can play the Semi-Tarrasch (4...c5) and take back on d5 with the knight to avoid an isolated pawn. We answer with e4 and get two strong centre pawns on d4 and e4; our plan is the d4-d5 break or a kingside attack. With 4.Bg5 (our main move), 4...c5 is met by 5.cxd5 cxd4 6.Qxd4 Be7 7.e3 and Black's d-pawn becomes isolated after ...exd5. lines.name: QGD 3...Bb4: 4.cxd5 exd5 5.Bf4

Other Black moves on move 3: 3...Nf6 4.Bxc4 e6 5.Nf3 transposes to the 3.Nf3 line, and 3...e6, 3...c5 or 3...a6 do the same after Bxc4 and Nf3; 3...e5 4.Bxc4 exd4 5.exd4 gives us free development. If Black avoids the blunder: 4...Bb7, 4...e6, 4...a6, 4...Nf6 or 4...e5 5.axb5; 4...bxa4 5.Qxa4+; 4...b4 5.Qf3! (the long-diagonal trick again); 5...e6, 5...Nf6, 5...Bb7 or 5...a6 6.Bxc4; 5...Bd7 6.bxc6 Nxc6 7.Nf3. In every case we win back the pawn with a much better game. After 6.Qf3 nothing saves Black: 6...Qc7, 6...a6 or 6...e6 7.Qxa8 wins a whole rook.

lines.name: Slav Main Line: 4...dxc4 5.a4 Bf5 6.e3 e6 7.Bxc4 Bb4 8.O-O

lines.name: Chebanenko Slav: 4...a6 5.e3 b5 6.b3
